  Guide to the City Commission Proceedings

The Oral Communication portion of the agenda is for members of the public to present items which are
not listed on the agenda, but are under the subject matter jurisdiction of the Commission. Although no
action may be taken, the Commission and staff will follow up, at an appropriate time, on those items
needing response. Each speaker is limited to three (3) minutes.

Items in Consent Calendar Section A have already been considered by the Commission at a previous
meeting where the public was invited to comment, after which a decision was made. These items are not
subject to public discussion at this meeting because the vote taken at the previous meeting was final.
 Youth Commission Regular Meeting Agenda  Page 3 of 3  December 4, 2025

Resolutions concerning decisions made at previous meetings are for the purpose of memorializing the
decision to assure the accuracy of the findings, the prior vote, and any conditions imposed.

Items in Consent Calendar Section B have not been discussed previously by the Commission. If
discussion is desired, an item may be removed from the Consent Calendar for individual
consideration. Commissioners may indicate a negative or abstaining vote on any individual item by so
declaring prior to the vote on the motion to adopt the entire Consent Calendar. Items excluded from the
Consent Calendar will be taken up by the Commission following the action on the Consent Calendar. The
Commission first will take up the items for which public speaker requests have been submitted. Public
speakers shall follow the rules as set forth under Oral Communication.

Old Business items have appeared on previous agendas but have either been continued or tabled to this
meeting with no final action having been taken. Public comment shall follow the rules as set forth under
Oral Communication.

Items in New Business are items which are appearing for the first time for formal action. Public comment
shall follow the rules as set forth under Oral Communication.

Copies of the staff reports or other written documentation relating to each item of business described
above are on file in the office of the City Manager, and available upon request by emailing
KManisco@malibucity.org.

The City Hall phone number is (310) 456-2489. To contact City Hall using a telecommunication device
for the deaf (TDD), please call (800) 735-2929 and a California Relay Service operator will assist you. In
compliance with the Americans with Disabilities Act, if you need special assistance to participate in this
meeting, please contact Yolanda Bundy, Environmental Sustainability Director, at (310) 456-2489, ext.
229. Notification 48 hours prior to the meeting will enable the City to make reasonable arrangements to
ensure accessibility to this meeting. [28 CFR 35.102-35.104 ADD Title II].

I hereby certify under penalty of perjury, under the laws of the State of California that the foregoing
agenda was posted in accordance with the applicable legal requirements. Dated this 1st day of December
2025 at 1:00 p.m.

ITEM 5  NEW BUSINESS

  A.  Youth Government Summit Series

  Recommended Action: Provide feedback on the topics and representatives for the
  Youth Government Summit Series.

  Recreation Manager Manisco presented the staff report.

  Chair Porat recommended a Park Ranger with experience from the Malibu region.

  Commissioner Webb suggested a speaker with expertise in environmental
  sustainability, resilience, or coastal preservation.

  Commissioner O’Herlihy suggested Los Angeles County Board of Supervisor,
  Lindsey P. Horvath, or an office representative.

  Commissioner Mirmohammadsadeghi recommended a college admissions

  B.  Health and Wellness Program

  Recommended Action: Provide feedback on the Health and Wellness Program.

  Recreation Manager Manisco presented the staff report.

  Commissioner K. Morra suggested fitness classes or a virtual presentation on the
  importance of fitness.

  Commissioner Magna recommended a yoga class.

  Commissioner Kaplan supported a run club or a run meet-up at a local park.

  Commissioner Mirmohammadsadeghi suggested a program with therapy dogs.

Commissioner Ovsiowitz arrived at 7:15 p.m.

  C.  Skate Park Grand Opening

  Recommended Action: Provide feedback on the event elements related to the
  Skate Park opening celebration.

  Recreation Manager Manisco presented the staff report.

  Commission O’Herlihy suggested non-local food vendors and professional skating

  Commissioner Kaplan recommended partnering with local skate businesses to
  provide merchandise giveaways.

  Commissioner Ovsiowitz recommended a raffle for merchandise giveaways.

  Commissioner Koziatek suggested a partnership with the Malibu Boys & Girls
  Club and the Johnny Strange Foundation.

  Commissioner Magna supported a skateboarding art activity with custom shirts and
  hats.

  Commissioner Mirmohammadsadeghi recommended a giveaway supply bag for
  new skaters, which would include wax and safety equipment.

Subject:  Community Service Learning Opportunities

RECOMMENDED ACTION: Discuss and approve in-person community service learning
opportunities from February through May 2026.

DISCUSSION: For several years, the Commission has organized volunteer opportunities
that benefit the community. From September 2020 through December 2023, the
Commission selected donation-based drives due to the pandemic-related constraints. In
2024-25, the Commission resumed in-person community service in combination with
donation drives.

At the September 4, 2025 Regular meeting, the Commission approved the following
volunteer days,
  • Malibu Moves Half-Marathon Volunteer Day, October 25, 2025
  • Beach Clean-Up Volunteer Day benefiting Heal the Bay, December 7, 2025

The Commission is asked to discuss and approve community service-learning
opportunities and schedules for the period from February to May 2026.

ATTACHMENTS: None.

Date prepared:  November 18, 2025  Meeting date: December 4, 2025

Subject:  Donation-Based Programs

RECOMMENDED ACTION: Discuss and approve non-profit beneficiaries receiving
contributions from Youth Commission donation drives from February through May 2026.

DISCUSSION: In 2020, the Commission initiated donation-based programs as an
alternative to in-person community service learning opportunities, in response to the
Pandemic. The donation-based programs were successful, and the Commission
expressed continued interest in maintaining community engagement by donating in-kind
items.

At the September 4, 2025 Regular meeting, the Commission approved the following
donation drives,
  • November 2025 - Canned Food Drive benefiting the Boys & Girls Club of Malibu
  • December 2025 - Toy Drive benefiting the Los Angeles County Firefighters
  Foundation

The Commission is asked to discuss non-profit beneficiaries who will receive
contributions from the Commission’s donation drives from February through May 2026.

Date prepared:  November 18, 2025  Meeting date: December 4, 2025

Subject:  Teen Outreach

RECOMMENDED ACTION: Provide feedback on teen outreach and communication
preferences.

DISCUSSION: The Youth Commission regularly reviews opportunities for teen outreach
and communication to increase attendance and awareness at programs and events.

Commissioners are asked to discuss methods to increase awareness of Commission
programs, activities, events, and community service-learning projects. Commissioners
may discuss the effectiveness of school announcements, on-campus events, in-person
marketing outreach, social media, website, and incentive-based marketing.

MOTION  Commissioner P. Polatin moved, and Commissioner K. Morra seconded a motion

  question was called, and the motion carried 19—0. Commissioners Hilling, Johnson,
  Jones, Kaplan, Koziatek, Mirmohammadsadeghi, Webb, and Wolski absent.

  Donation-Based Programs

  Recommended Action: Discuss and approve non-profit beneficiaries receiving
  contributions from Youth Commission donation drives from February through

  Recreation Manager Manisco presented the staff report.

  Commissioner Myers suggested a blanket and towel donation drive to benefit the
  Agoura Animal Care Center.

  Commissioner P. Polatin indicated agreement with Commissioner Myers.

  Commissioner Magna recommended a blanket and towel donation drive to benefit
  the people of Kenya, Africa.

  Chair Porat stated that the Commission must figure out the mailing logistics for a
  donation to Kenya, Africa.

  Commissioner Ovsiowitz suggested a sports equipment donation drive benefitting
  the Boys & Girls Club of Malibu.

  Commissioner O’Herlihy recommended a skateboard donation drive corresponding
  with the grand opening of the Malibu Skate Park.

  Commissioner Aragon stated she would support a sports equipment and skateboard
  equipment into a single donation drive.

MOTION  Commissioner P. Polatin moved, and Commissioner O’Herlihy seconded a motion
  to host a blanket and towel donation drive, benefiting the Agoura Animal Care
